data.title: Desloratadine
data.summary: Antihistamines · Second-generation H1 antihistamine — active metabolite of loratadine
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antihistamines_

**Class:** Second-generation H1 antihistamine — active metabolite of loratadine

## Mechanism of action
- Highly potent selective peripheral H1 inverse agonist; some anti-inflammatory effect

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Chronic urticaria, allergic rhinitis

## Dose & formulations
- 5 mg once daily (updosing up to 20 mg in urticaria); children 6–11 years 2.5 mg

## Adverse effects
- Headache, fatigue; non-sedating at standard dose

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity to loratadine

## Drug interactions
- Minimal; erythromycin/ketoconazole raise levels without QT change

## Pregnancy & lactation
Limited data; loratadine preferred.

## Viva points
- Active metabolite of loratadine; long half-life (~27 h)

_Sources: Khopkar (Second generation H1 antihistamines); Wolverton 4e ch.32. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
